record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.context_brief: Non-commuting spectral and tail dependence theory
record.original_question: Create a multivariate spectral theory for tuples of non-commuting normal operators and use it to introduce non-commutative tail-dependence measures in non-commutative C*-algebras and operator spaces.

evidence.quote: (3-RP2) Create a “multivariate” spectral theory of non-commuting normal operator tuples and introduce non-commutative tail dependency measures in non-commutative C ∗-algebras and operator spaces.

artifact.category_tag: non-commutative spectral theory and tail dependence
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a bounded operator $N$ on a Hilbert space is called normal if $N N^* = N^* N$, and that the classical spectral theorem provides a projection-valued measure on the spectrum $\sigma(N) \subset \mathbb{C}$ representing $N$. For a finite tuple $(N_1, \dots, N_d)$ of pairwise commuting normal operators there is a joint projection-valued measure on $\mathbb{C}^d$, which underlies a multivariate functional calculus. In the classical (commutative) probabilistic setting, tail-dependence measures (such as upper and lower tail-dependence coefficients of a copula) quantify the asymptotic probability that one coordinate of a random vector takes an extreme value given that another coordinate does.

The problem has two intertwined parts:

(a) Develop a multivariate spectral theory for tuples $(N_1, \dots, N_d)$ of normal elements in a unital C*-algebra (or for tuples of normal operators on a Hilbert space, or normal elements of an operator space) that are not assumed to commute. Specifically, define an appropriate notion of joint spectrum and a functional calculus that reduces to the standard joint spectral theorem when the $N_i$ pairwise commute, and that is rich enough to support analytic and measure-theoretic operations on the joint spectral data of non-commuting normal tuples.

(b) Using this spectral framework, define non-commutative analogues of tail-dependence measures for tuples of normal elements in C*-algebras and operator spaces, generalizing the classical tail-dependence coefficients of probability theory, and establish their basic properties (e.g.\ invariance, monotonicity, behaviour under tensor products, and reduction to the classical tail-dependence measures in the commutative case).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad research program (creating a non-commutative multivariate spectral theory and corresponding tail-dependence measures). No web evidence indicates that such a theory has been completed; multivariate joint spectral theory for non-commuting normal tuples remains an active and unresolved area, and non-commutative tail-dependence measures in C*-algebras/operator spaces do not appear to have been systematically developed.
